t.1.75.1: Having then heard those words of Jāmadagnya, Dāśarathi, whose speech had been restrained out of reverence for his father, spoke to Rāma.
t.1.75.2: I have heard of the deed you performed, O Bhārgava. We respect it, O brahman, for you were intent on repaying your debt to your father.
t.1.75.4: Having spoken thus, the enraged Rāghava, swift in his prowess, took from the hand of Bhārgava that excellent weapon and the arrow as well.
t.1.75.3: O Bhārgava, I scorn one who is, as it were, devoid of valor and powerless in the duty of a kṣatriya; behold today my might and my prowess.
t.1.75.5: Having strung the bow, Rāma fitted an arrow to its string. Then Rāma, enraged, spoke these words to Rāma Jāmadagnya.
t.1.75.6: Because you are a brāhmaṇa, and also for the sake of Viśvāmitra, you are worthy of my reverence; therefore, O Rāma, I cannot release at you this life-taking arrow.
t.1.75.7: O Rāma, I shall destroy whichever you wish: either this power of movement of yours, or the incomparable worlds you have won through the strength of your austerities.
t.1.75.8: For this divine arrow of Viṣṇu, conqueror of enemy cities, destroyer of strength and pride, does not fall in vain through its might.
t.1.75.9: To see Rāma, bearer of the finest weapon, the gods together with the hosts of seers, placing Pitāmaha at their head, assembled there in throngs.
t.1.75.10: Gandharvas and Apsarases, Siddhas, Cāraṇas and Kiṃnaras, Yakṣas, Rākṣasas and Nāgas too gathered to behold that great wonder.
t.1.75.12: Jāmadagnya, rendered numb by Rāma's splendour because his own valour had been struck down, spoke very softly to lotus-petal-eyed Rāma.
t.1.75.11: Then, when the world had been struck motionless and Rāma held the excellent bow, that Jāmadagnya Rāma, drained of his might, gazed up at Rāma.
t.1.75.13: When long ago I gave the earth to Kāśyapa, Kāśyapa said to me, "You must not dwell within my domain."
t.1.75.14: So I, carrying out the word of my guru, do not dwell upon the earth for a single night. This promise, O Kākutstha, was indeed made by me to Kāśyapa.
t.1.75.15: Therefore, O heroic Rāghava, you should not destroy this power of movement of mine. Swift as thought, I shall go to Mahendra, the best of mountains.
t.1.75.16: But the incomparable worlds that I have won through austerity, O Rāma, destroy them with this finest of arrows; let there be no lapse of time.
t.1.75.17: From your handling of this bow I know you to be the imperishable slayer of Madhu, the lord of the gods. May there be well-being for you, O scorcher of foes!
t.1.75.18: All these hosts of gods, gathered together, are watching you, whose deeds are matchless and who have no rival in battle.
t.1.75.19: O Kākutstha, this should be no cause of shame for me, that I have been turned back by you, the lord of the three worlds.
t.1.75.20: O Rāma, you of excellent vows, you should release this matchless arrow; when the arrow is released, I shall go to Mahendra, the finest of mountains.
t.1.75.21: While Rāma Jāmadagnya was speaking thus, the glorious and mighty Rāma Dāśarathi discharged the excellent arrow.
t.1.75.22: Then all the directions and the intermediate directions likewise became free of darkness, and the gods together with the hosts of sages praised Rāma, who held his weapon raised aloft.
t.1.75.23: Rāma Jāmadagnya, the mighty lord, having praised Rāma Dāśarathi and then circumambulated him, went his own way.
